title: Dissociation and flow cytometric isolation of murine intestinal epithelial cells for multi-omic profiling
protocol: Euthanize mouse by cervical dislocation or other approved method.
Expose the abdominal cavity of the euthanized mouse.
Make a V-shape incision with scissors to cut away skin and expose the abdominal cavity.
Collect ileum tissues.
Cut the colon from the anus and gently pull out the intestine from the abdominal cavity.
Cut the end of the small intestine from the cecum.
Remove fat and mesentery tissues from dissected ileum with tweezers.
Flush away luminal contents using cold DPBS with an animal feeding needle.
Cut open the ileum longitudinally using scissors.
Place tissues in a 50 mL falcon tube pre-filled with 10 mL of cold DPBS.
Keep the tube on ice until all animals are processed.
Wash the tissue three times with cold DPBS.
Remove DPBS by pouring it out.
Add 10 mL of cold DPBS and shake the tube up and down for 20–30 seconds.
Repeat steps to wash the tissue two more times.
Transfer tissue to a petri dish.
Slice tissue into small fragments roughly 2–3 cm in length.
Transfer tissue fragments into a 15 mL falcon tube pre-filled with 7 mL of cold EDTA buffer.
Keep the tube on ice.
Shake the tube by hand (up and down) every 7–8 minutes, approximately 60 cycles in total at 0.5 seconds per cycle.
Incubate the tube on ice for 30 minutes.
Shake the tube vigorously for 2 minutes after the initial incubation period.
Use a tweezer to remove tissues from the tube.
Centrifuge at 500 g and 4°C for 5 minutes; discard supernatant.
Add 10 mL of cold DPBS to wash cell pellets.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 500 g and 4°C for 5 minutes again.
Remove the supernatant using pipette tips.
Immediately add 2 mL TrypLE Express Enzyme to resuspend cell pellets gently with a 1 mL pipette tip.
Incubate the mixture at 22°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Pipette up and down 10 times with a 1 mL pipette every 3-4 minutes during incubation to break cell aggregates gently.
Fill the tube with 10 mL of cold DPBS.
Pass through a 70 μm cell strainer placed on a 50 mL falcon tube, collecting all flow-through (single-cell suspension).
Centrifuge at 500 g and 4°C for 5 minutes to pellet cells.
Resuspend cells using 1 mL of Live/Dead staining solution (1:1000 dilution in DPBS) for cell surface staining.
Transfer the stained cells to FACS tubes and keep them in a 4°C fridge for 20 minutes.
Wash cells by adding 4 mL of cold DPBS to the tube; spin down to remove supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 300 μL of FcR blocking reagent (1:50 dilution in FACS buffer); keep at 4°C for 5 min.
Dilute antibodies (anti-CD45, anti-CD31, anti-TER-119 and anti-EpCAM) into FACS buffer (1:50 dilution).
Add 300 μL of antibody cocktail to the cells (1:100 final dilution); gently vortex; keep at 4°C for 30 min.
Wash cells by adding 4 mL of cold FACS buffer; spin down at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min; remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 300 μL of MACS buffer and transfer to FACS tubes with 35 μm cell strainer cap; keep on ice.
Mix cells with AOPI staining solution at a 1:1 ratio.
Load 20 μL onto slide and count using Auto 2000.
After cell counting, immediately proceed to downstream analysis.
If cells are used for bulk RNA-seq, spin down the cells at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min.
Carefully remove supernatant by pipetting; resuspend cell pellets in 350 μL of Buffer RLT Plus supplemented with 1% β-mercaptoethanol.
Pause point: samples can be stored at −80°C for months until being further processed for RNA isolation using RNeasy Micro Plus kit.
Wear a mask when handling β-mercaptoethanol.
If cells are used for single-cell RNA-seq, immediately proceed to GEM generation and barcoding.
Spin down the cells at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min.
Carefully remove supernatant by pipetting.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL cold DPBS and transfer to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for washing.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min.
Completely remove the supernatants.
Cells can be snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen or on dry ice.
Store snap-frozen cells at -80°C for metabolite extraction.
